verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in a chariot, caught between two armies, asking what he must do. Krishna tells him that every duty has flaws, and no path is perfect. The better choice is to walk the path that fits your own nature, even if you stumble. Doing the work born of who you are, without copying another, brings no wrong. It is not about the family name you carry, but about the honest fit of your own hand to the task.
verse.for_you: You are making flat whites and sending out applications, but your mind keeps drifting to other people's wins. Today, notice when that happens. Let the comparison be there. Then bring your attention back to the work in your hands, the one that fits you. Do that imperfectly, and let it be enough.

verse.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verse.setting: Kakbhushundi continues listing the diseases of the mind.
verse.sanskrit: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥
verse.line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
verse.translation: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verse.why: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

prasang.title: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

verse.meaning: Kakbhushundi is speaking to Garuda, describing the sicknesses that live inside the mind. He names envy as an itch that burns when you see another person happy. He calls the joy and pain of comparing yourself to others a sickness of the throat. He says that the heat you feel at someone else's success is a wasting disease. He wants you to know these feelings by name, to see them clearly as they are.
verse.for_you: You feel the heat when you see someone else's win. That is not a sign of your failure. It is simply the itch Kakbhushundi names. You do not have to feed it or hide from it. Just notice the itch, and let it be.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verse.sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
verse.translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
verse.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasang.title: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna how the wise move through the world. He says that a person who is content with what arrives without asking, who stays beyond the swings of success and failure, and who is free from envy, remains unbound even while doing their work. This is the state of those who act without selfish motive, steady in joy and sorrow, dependent on nothing.
verse.for_you: You are making flat whites while your mother tells the aunties you are exploring. Your own life is right there in your hands. Let their chatter about your options pass. Your path is not less because theirs looks bigger. Keep your eyes on the cup you are pouring.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verse.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verse.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
verse.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
verse.why: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.
verse.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.

prasang.title: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about the one who is close to him, the one who is dear to God. This person does not let blame or praise change their mind. They are quiet, content with what comes, and do not stay fixed in one place. They are steady in their mind, not looking for status or praise. Their devotion is constant. The idea is that you can be kind and steady without hating. You do not have to chase praise or run from blame. That steadiness is what is loved.
verse.for_you: The applications you sent and the flat whites you make are your path. When your mother tells the aunties, let the words pass. Your worth is not in their ears. You do not need to match their wins to have ground beneath your feet. Be steady in what comes.

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
verse.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.
verse.translation: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.meaning: In Mithila, a meat-seller named Dharmavyadha teaches a proud ascetic named Kaushika that true goodness is simple. He says a person free of envy and full of gratitude naturally finds happiness, right living, and prosperity. The butcher points out that wisdom is not hidden in forests but lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work with honesty. The teaching is to let go of envy, repent for harm done, and care for your parents.
verse.for_you: try to let go of the comparison for just one day. While you make those flat whites, focus only on the steam and the cup in your hands. Do not let anyone else's path distract you from the work of this one hour.

verse.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verse.setting: The sage warns the deposed prince against resenting others' success.
verse.sanskrit: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा / अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते नराः / अभिनिष्यन्दते देही श्रीभूतश्च द्विषज्जनात्
verse.line: Make peace with other people's success, even when you lack it. The wise can enjoy good fortune that isn't theirs.
verse.translation: Bear the good fortune of others, even though it is not with you. Wise people know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else; good fortune drains away from the one who resents.
verse.why: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

He says the wise know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else. The one who resents another's success only loses their own vitality. story.title: Shuka at Janaka's gate
story.story_hook: Shuka stood at King Janaka's gate for seven days, and no one came to let him in.
story.summary: Young Shuka, already wise, is sent by his father Vyasa to King Janaka. Janaka ignores him at the gate for seven days, then lets him wait in the courtyard seven more, then surrounds him with luxury for seven days. Shuka stays exactly the same throughout, and Janaka bows to him.
story.lesson: Steadiness is proved when neither neglect nor luxury moves you.

anchor.speaker: Narrator
anchor.setting: Shuka is kept waiting at King Janaka's gate, then tested with luxury.
anchor.sanskrit: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम् ॥ केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः ॥
anchor.line: Ignored for days, then pampered with luxury, Shuka stayed the same, steady as a mountain in a breeze.
anchor.translation: Those pleasures and those foods did not move the mind of Vyasa's son, as a gentle breeze cannot move a mountain on its base. Only even, clear, silent and glad of heart, complete like the full moon, pure Shuka remained.
anchor.why: Steadiness is proved when neither neglect nor luxury moves you.

weeks.title: The weight of being left behind

script: You are between things right now. You send out applications and make flat whites, and your mother tells aunties that you are exploring options. But inside, you are stuck and ashamed. You keep looking at other people's wins and your own life disappears behind it.
Arjuna stands in a chariot, caught between two armies, asking what he must do. Krishna tells him that every duty has flaws, and no path is perfect. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

The idea is simple and hard. Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering. You do not need to do it perfectly. You do not need to match someone else's standard. Every path has cracks. The only wrong thing is to force yourself onto a path that is not yours.

When you are making a flat white, let your hand know the cup. When you send an application, let it be your own. Let the comparison be there, and then let it go. Bring your attention back to the work in your hands.
What is the one thing in front of you right now?

depth.life: You are making flat whites and sending out applications, but your mind drifts to other people's wins. You feel ashamed and stuck, as if your own life is disappearing behind everyone else's success.
depth.points: You are not stuck because you cannot get in. You are stuck because every time you look, someone else's win is the only thing you see, and your own life disappears behind it.
depth.practice: Notice when your mind compares you to others today. Then bring your attention back to the work in your hands, the one that fits you.
depth.question: What is one small thing you did today that fits your own nature?
